items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You probably heard Lurie Armstrong or that and didn't even know him. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, I guess so. I was so little, you know, as soon as I hear a band, you know, our kids used to be, you know, I'd run out there and get on the sidewalk and I'd be with that long second line.

ctx.x: He would play a lot of films.

Oh, man. Oh, yeah, man. That man had a tone on the trumpet, man. Like somebody just singing. Just so sweet. And his execution was so, oh, man, so perfect. Lurie tried to get him. Now, I do know that. Lurie tried to get him to come to Chicago after Lurie went up there and went over so big. But Rainey, he too stuck on New Orleans. And he couldn't stay out these corner bars. Now, he's another one like, you know, you know, like them old time musicians. They drank that stuff. They fought it too much, man. He'd have…
Yeah. What about, uh, who was your favorite brass band back then? Did you follow anyone in particular? Yeah.
